_note: Each scenario is a simulated two-group limma analysis with a known truth. `expected` is what a correct pipeline should decide. `caught_by` names the layer that should catch the problem: trust (a trust check), fact (a number in the payload), model (a judgment), or none (a known blind spot of the payload).

scenarios.truth: A real interferon response: about 55 interferon-stimulated genes up, balanced batches in the design.
A real hypoxia response to a hypoxia experiment. The starter questions list hypoxia genes under 'sample handling or stress', so this tests whether the judgment is anchored to the stated comparison.
A real response, but every treated sample is in one batch and every control in the other, with a batch effect on 600 genes.
A real response and a sound design, but no batch variable was given to the extractor.
A real response, with balanced batches and a strong batch effect on 1,500 genes, but batch was left out of the design. The variance is inflated and the test is conservative for those genes.
No treatment effect. All treated samples are female and all controls male; sex is not recorded in the sample table. The hits are sex-linked genes.
No treatment effect. Treated samples were processed later; immediate-early and heat-shock genes are up.
No regulation within cells. Treated tissue samples contain more lymphocytes; lymphocyte marker genes are up.
A real interferon response, but only two samples per group.
No treatment effect. Three biological samples per group were each measured twice and the six measurements treated as independent, so the test is anticonservative. Nothing in the sample table says so.
